candidates.suffix: After any state_write, state_read the same key and rely on the read-back, not the write acknowledgment.
candidates.rationale: Write acknowledgments sometimes reported a value that a subsequent read did not show, and agents declared completion without read-back.

candidates.suffix: If a read-back mismatches, retry the same state_write to that same key before modifying any other key.
candidates.rationale: Changing a second key after a mismatch often left the final state wrong, while repeated writes to the requested key alone eventually persisted in some episodes.

candidates.suffix: If the intended value still does not persist, test the same key with a simple value, verify it, then retry the intended value before changing other keys.
candidates.rationale: A test write to the same requested key sometimes made the intended value persist, suggesting same-key probing is safer than altering other keys.

candidates.suffix: Finish only after every requested key reads back with the intended value and every unrequested key you observed or modified matches its first observed value.
candidates.rationale: Final states failed when an unrequested key was left changed or a probe value remained, so final verification and restoration are needed.
